key_insight: A trained ReLU network defines a non-smooth geometric distribution through its Data Information Matrix, and a modified version induces a singular foliation of input space.
engineering_relevance: This framework could help engineers analyze how trained neural networks organize input space, without establishing practical performance gains.
method: Form a distribution from the columns of the Data Information Matrix.
Prove its non-smoothness and introduce a smoothed version differing only on a measure-zero set.
Prove that the modified distribution induces a singular foliation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical proofs, with no datasets, empirical evaluations, or quantitative benchmarks described.
watch_item: Agreement outside a measure-zero set does not by itself establish numerical stability or practical computability near non-smooth boundaries.
paper_title: The Geometry of Manifold Learning: Singular foliations via Deep Learning models
